methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $105M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
EarthGrid is a Seed-stage transportation company that has raised $105.3M to date. The valuation comp universe consists of six private frontier-transport companies including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and Olympian Motors; no public comparables exist in this nascent segment.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($105M) as a proxy for implied post-Seed valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A transitions yields $263M. This method grounds the analysis in the company's demonstrated capital absorption and historical stage-progression patterns observed across early-stage transportation ventures.

Peer-median comparison is not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer coverage. While three Transportation-sector companies exist in the available comp set, none meet same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier filters required for reliable median derivation. A broader all-sector median would introduce excessive methodological noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $224M (low) to $303M (median) with central estimate at $263M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression point estimate, accounting for execution risk and limited comparables. Key uncertainties include path to Series A fundraising success, actual capital efficiency relative to peer benchmarks, and the durability of frontier-transportation investor appetite. The single-method foundation warrants heightened sensitivity to stage-progression multiplier assumptions.
